classification.difficultyReason: Form and solve a surface-area equation for the prism length, then explain why doubling that length doubles only the rectangular areas while the triangular ends remain unchanged.

content.prompt: This prism has surface area $222\text{ cm}^2$.

spec.description: Unshaded oblique triangular prism. Both rear triangular sloping sides have external 5 cm dimension arrows; the front base is 8 cm, its perpendicular height is 3 cm, and a longitudinal edge is x cm. The rear base is dashed.
spec.answerVisibility: All dimensions are permanent student givens; no answer is shown.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The prism length is doubled from $11\text{ cm}$ to $22\text{ cm}$. Find its new surface area.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain why this is $24\text{ cm}^2$ less than twice the original surface area.

answer.short: The rectangular areas double, but the two triangular ends keep their combined area of $24\text{ cm}^2$.
answer.worked: Twice the original surface area counts the triangular ends twice: $2(222)-24=420\text{ cm}^2$. Only the rectangular face areas double.
